title: Emrys and the Ember
premise: Noor Lockridge has spent twenty years keeping the Ember Gate sealed, the last working threshold between the mortal realm of Thornfell and the god-realm of Cindral, where the old gods were banished after a war of broken oaths. When prayers begin to be answered—small mercies at first, then miracles with a price—Noor realizes the gate is failing and something on the other side is reaching through, something that remembers Noor's grandmother helped seal it. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors, who blame the returning gods for a spreading blight, and courted by a fugitive godling named Sef who claims to want the covenant restored, Noor must gather the scattered Ember Shards and reforge the covenant at the gate itself. In the end, Noor learns the covenant never required a gate at all—only a keeper willing to stand between—and they choose to become the living threshold, saving both realms at the cost of never fully belonging to either.
about_author: Marguerite Yarrow is a former trail-crew cook in the northern ranges who writes fantasy about borders, both drawn and felt. She lives in a converted fire lookout with two dogs and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor Lockridge, POV. Noor inspects the Ember Gate on its centennial check, finding hairline cracks and a warmth that shouldn't exist. They note it in the ledger, tell no one. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a vigil no one knows matters, and the first flicker of dread.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the village of Lowmarsh, a drowned child is brought back breathing after her mother prays to a god outlawed for a century. Noor recognizes the old rites from their grandmother's banned prayer book. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as the impossible becomes local.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Through
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, first appearance. A godling in mortal flesh stumbles out of the mountains near the gate, burned and half-starved, and is taken in by Noor under a smuggler's pretense. Sef observes Noor's careful routines, hiding what he is. Emotional beat: wary fascination between two people both pretending to be smaller than they are.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Crown inquisitors arrive in Lowmarsh investigating the miracle, led by the methodical, genuinely pious Vane. Noor lies smoothly about the mountains and hates how good they've become at it. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility—every lie is a brick in the wall between Noor and their neighbors.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The gate flares during a storm; touching it, Noor receives a fragmented memory—their grandmother, younger, sealing the gate alongside a god who wept. Noor realizes the covenant wasn't destroyed, it was deferred. Emotional beat: grief for a family history built on a buried promise.

chapters.title: Sef's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Cornered by Noor's questions, Sef reveals himself: a minor god of thresholds, exiled with the others, who slipped through the failing gate to find a keeper of Lockridge blood. He offers truth and alliance; Noor offers suspicion. Emotional beat: the dangerous relief of finally telling someone the truth.

chapters.title: The Blight
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The answered prayers carry a price: crops in Lowmarsh gray and crumble where miracles touched them. Vane declares the gods' return a plague and imposes martial law. Emotional beat: Noor's guilt—they kept the gate, and the gate is the wound.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Noor and Sef's POV, alternating. Noor leads Sef through the Thornfell passes toward the first Ember Shard, hidden in a ruined shrine, pursued by Vane's riders. Sef is humbled by mortal endurance. Emotional beat: grudging trust forged on dangerous ground.

chapters.title: The First Shard
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the drowned shrine of Vessa, Noor takes the First Shard and is flooded with the memory of the covenant's original terms: the gods would keep the land, mortals would keep the gods honest. Both sides broke it. Emotional beat: disillusionment—there are no innocent parties, only abandoned duties.

chapters.title: The Burning of Lowmarsh
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. A miracle-gone-wrong ignites the village granaries. Vane, grieving a son lost to a false prayer, orders the shrine district purged. Emotional beat: the tragedy of righteous men—the inquisitor is not a villain but a wound given authority.

chapters.title: Refugees on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor's hidden roads fill with Lowmarsh refugees fleeing Vane's purge. Noor must choose between secrecy and shelter, and chooses people over the mission, revealing the gate's existence to the community. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last, at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. One refugee, a shrine-keeper's widow, sells the gate's location to Vane to buy her children's freedom. Sef catches her and, to Noor's horror, lets her go—his first act of mortal mercy. Emotional beat: the corrupting logic of necessity tested and refused.

chapters.title: Vane at the Gate
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane reaches the Ember Gate with sappers and scripture, intending to collapse it forever and end the gods' reach. Noor stands in the doorway of worlds and refuses to move. Emotional beat: a standoff between two keepers of different covenants—the law's justice against the older kind.

chapters.title: The Second Shard
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The standoff breaks when the gate convulses; in the chaos Noor seizes the Second Shard from the gate's own heart, and Vane, seeing the memory it carries, wavers for the first time. Emotional beat: an enemy shown the same grief, and the fragile pause it opens.

chapters.title: What Waits Behind
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Through the cracked gate, Sef makes contact with the exiled pantheon—and discovers the eldest god, Ossuar, has been consuming the others' power to force the gate open, and that Sef was sent as a lure. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own heaven; the shattering of a cause.

chapters.title: The Widow's Road
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The traitor widow returns, bringing Vane's secret route maps as penance. Noor must decide whether forgiveness is a debt or a gift, and chooses gift. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—mercy as an act of strength, not weakness.

chapters.title: Assembly at the Gate
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor convenes refugees, the wavering Vane, and Sef before the failing gate and lays out the truth: Ossuar is coming, the covenant can be reforged, and it will cost a keeper everything. Volunteers step forward. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; Noor stops being invisible by choice.

chapters.title: The Night of Ash
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ossuar breaches the gate in a storm of ash; the refugees hold the passes, Vane turns his inquisitors against the god he once blamed, and Sef is nearly unmade buying time. Emotional beat: the climax's opening—sacrifice stacked on sacrifice, hope thin as a blade.

chapters.title: The Third Shard
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Inside the collapsing gate, Noor finds the Third Shard held in Ossuar's grip and learns the final term of the covenant: it requires a living keeper to bind it. Noor takes the shard from a god's burning hand. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the price made plain.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Threshold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, the climax. At the gate's heart, Noor speaks the old covenant aloud, binds the three shards into their own body, and becomes the living threshold—neither god nor mortal, a door that chooses whom to open for. Ossuar is sealed not by force but by terms. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-sacrifice; the loneliest victory.

chapters.title: After the Ash
chapters.summary: Vane's and Sef's POV. Vane dissolves the inquisition's mandate over the mountains and files a report no one will believe; Sef stays as the gate-keeper's voice, teaching Lowmarsh to pray honestly again. Emotional beat: mourning and repair—the world remade smaller and kinder.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. A year later, Noor stands at the gate that is now themselves, greeting pilgrims from both realms, belonging to neither and needed by both. Sef brings tea; the ledger has a new first line. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—home redefined as the place you stand for others.
